workflows.title: MiniMax H3 Reference
workflows.description: MiniMax H3 conditioned on up to nine reference pictures, three reference videos and three reference audio clips instead of a start/end frame — the model's Reference mode. Subjects, clothing, environments and styles are carried across from the pictures; a reference video carries MOTION — how a body moves, gesticulates and holds its mannerisms and expressions — and how literally it is copied is set by the prompt's retention_analysis tag for that <Video k>, from fully_preserved (reproduce this motion) down through attribute_transfer (a different action performed in this performer's manner) to weak_reference (loose pacing cue); each reference video may also carry its own soundtrack. A reference audio clip clones a VOICE (or music) — either reperforming its exact dialogue or lending only its timbre and delivery to new lines. Audio clips must be 2-15s each, 15s combined, and always ride alongside at least one picture or video. Reference videos are read as 24 fps, are trimmed to the generated clip's own length, and their tokens ride through every sampling step, so they cost real time. The prompt follows MiniMax's full-reference format (subject_definitions, retention_analysis, <Subject N>/<Picture N>/<Video N>/<Audio N> labels). Same weights and same rented lane as MiniMax H3, so no re-provisioning.

prompt_contract.guidance: Reference mode uses MiniMax's full-reference rewrite format (ref_en): six sections in order — subject_definitions (label every reference as <Subject N> / <Picture N> / <Video N>), summary, retention_analysis (fully_preserved | partially_preserved | attribute_transfer | weak_reference per label), detailed_description (shots, <d>[English] …</d> speech, (S1) ids), overall_soundscape, non_diegetic_music. Reference pictures are supplied in order, so <Picture 1> is the first image sent. Reference videos are labeled <Video N> in their own supplied order. A reference video is a MOTION reference: retention_analysis decides how literally it binds — fully_preserved reproduces the movement itself, partially_preserved keeps its broad shape, attribute_transfer performs a DIFFERENT action in that performer's manner (gesticulation style, posture, mannerisms, facial expressiveness), weak_reference is a loose pacing or rhythm cue. Say which subject inherits it ('<Subject 1> (S1) moves with the gesture style of <Video 1>.'). Reference audio clips are labeled <Audio N>, numbered independently of pictures and videos — but a reference video's OWN soundtrack also takes an <Audio N> label, emitted before its <Video N>, so a video-with-sound plus one standalone voice clip numbers as <Audio 1> (the video's track), <Video 1>, then <Audio 2> (the voice clip). Define each in subject_definitions ('<Audio 1> is the voice-timbre reference for <Subject 1> (S1).'), tag the summary [audio reuse] when the source words are reperformed verbatim (keep them, original language, inside <d>…</d>) or [audio reference] when only timbre/rhythm/emotion carries (then the source's own words must NOT appear), and mark each <Audio N> in retention_analysis with fully_copy | partially_copy | reference | weak_reference.

workflows.title: MiniMax H3
workflows.description: MiniMax H3 omni-modal video generation: video and native stereo audio (voice, SFX, music) are denoised jointly in one pass. Text-to-video by default; supply a start image for image-to-video. Runs on an H3-capable CUDA Comfy lane (pruned int8_convrot DiT + Qwen3-VL 32B nvfp4 encoder, ComfyUI >= e377e263 with the Spectrum forecaster node — see packages/gpu-rentals). Native canvas is a 768px short edge at 24 fps, up to ~15s on the 17k+5 frame grid. Spectrum forecasting is on by default and can be switched off per generation: it predicts about half the transformer steps instead of computing them, which roughly halves sampling time but softens fine detail. Three optional accelerators ride the same graph, all OFF by default and lifted out of the chain entirely when unset, so the default path is unchanged. Measured on a rented RTX 5090 (5s @ 960x544, warm, fixed seed, ComfyUI's own per-prompt timing): no acceleration 60.3s; spectrum (the default) 39.1s; solattn_tau 1.3 34.3s — NVlabs sparse attention chained onto sage, 11% faster than spectrum at equal-or-better detail and the same take, needs the pinned SolAttn Triton node and pays ~6s of kernel autotune on the first run of a process; easycache 0.2-0.3 41.9s. easycache and spectrum CANNOT combine — the forecaster disables itself whenever a cache wrapper patches the same model — and the choice between them is about fidelity, not speed: easycache lands 28-35 dB from the unaccelerated render where spectrum lands ~20 dB, i.e. spectrum reaches a visibly different take at the same seed. interpolate 2 runs core RIFE over the decoded frames for 24 -> 48 fps at +2.9s (3 gives 72 fps at +4.0s), leaving clip duration and the sampled frame count alone.

motion_reference_budget.measured: 2026-08-15, rented RTX 5090 (32607MiB), ComfyUI 0.32.0 with the cudaMallocAsync allocator, MiniMax H3 reference mode at 704x1216 with nine pictures and a voice clip throughout. The node trims a reference to min(its own length, the clip's length) — frames[:frame_count] in comfy_extras/nodes_minimax_h3.py — so the cost follows that EFFECTIVE reference length, not the clip's. Measured effective lengths: 48f ran (27.88GiB, reproduced twice), 96f ran (29.13GiB), 158f ran (30.06GiB), 243f ran (28.78GiB), 305f ran OUT OF MEMORY. 704*1216*243 = 208023552. Supersedes a 2026-08-13 reading of 141f, taken before this allocator: 158f was recorded as OOM there and runs here, and the per-reference-frame cost is ~0.9GiB across 48->243f rather than the ~15GiB that reading implied. Re-measure on a new box or allocator.

prompt_contract.guidance: H3 was trained on the structured rewrite its authors' pipeline emits (docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_base_en.md), so the format is part of the interface. Send three fields in order, blank-line separated: 'integrated_multimodal_description:' (open with one style/composition sentence, then numbered shots — '[Shot 1]' with no timestamp, later shots '[Shot N] At MM:SS.mmm,'; stable speaker ids (S1),(S2); speech in <d>[English] the exact words</d>, marked <cutoff> if still running at the end; camera moves as prose naming move, distance and speed), 'overall_soundscape:' (1-4 sentences of ambience and action sound, never dialogue), 'non_diegetic_music:' (1-3 sentences or N/A). With a start image, open with the anchor line 'For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.' H3 has no negative conditioning: state everything affirmatively.

workflows.title: MiniMax H3 Image
workflows.description: MiniMax H3 as a STILL image generator, through H3 Studio's FL2VA/REF2VA paths. H3 was never released as an image model: it decodes a short clip and a frame selector picks the still out of it, which is why the graph carries seconds/fps it cannot change. Text-to-image by default; attach up to nine ordered references (addressed @Image1..@Image9, the same grammar the video reference lane already speaks) to run the REF2VA path. Runs on the same rented H3 box as the video lanes — lane_needles already match its weights.
